title: SEC-001: Sanitize Content-Disposition header filename
description: The Content-Disposition header is parsed with a simple regex and used directly as a filename without sanitization. An attacker could craft a filename with path traversal characters (../) or special characters to cause issues. This is a security vulnerability that must be fixed before merge.

context.current_code:
const match = disposition.match(/filename=(.+)$/)
const filename = match ? match[1] : 'ArcVault-Setup.exe'
context.issue: No validation or sanitization of filename from Content-Disposition header

acceptance_criteria: Filename regex rejects path separators (/ and \\)
Filename is sanitized to allow only safe characters (alphanumeric, dash, underscore, dot)
Special characters are replaced with underscore
Test with special chars: evil<>.exe, evil|.exe, evil".exe
All tests pass; legitimate filenames still work

implementation_notes.regex_update: Change from /filename=(.+)$/ to /filename=([^\/\\]+)$/ to reject path separators
implementation_notes.example_code:
const match = disposition.match(/filename=([^\/\\]+)$/)
const filename = match
  ? match[1].replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/g, '_')
  : 'ArcVault-Setup.exe'

manual_test: Download installer and verify filename is correct
Check browser DevTools Network tab for Content-Disposition header
Verify file downloads with expected name

rollback_plan: git revert <commit-hash> — isolated change, safe to revert
notes: This is a security fix and must be merged before other fixes. Path traversal could allow arbitrary file placement on user system.
